title: Measuring the Effects of Data Parallelism on Neural Network Training
abstract: We study the relationship between training speed and the number of workers in synchronous data-parallel neural network training. We examine factors that affect the relationship between batch size and the number of gradient steps required to reach a target error. We find that all neural networks in our study contain a regime where batch size can be scaled without degrading model quality, but this 'perfect scaling' regime ends at a critical batch size. We also find that beyond the critical batch size, larger batches are less compute efficient. We characterize the boundaries of perfect scaling as a function of dataset, model architecture, and optimizer, shedding light on the factors that limit the benefit of additional parallelism.
